accounting.rationale: Original physical PDF120, printed106, lines20-21 defines the entity as a variable and permits asynchronous I/O or communication. It does not require an operation, actual concurrent execution or an optimization strategy.
An ASYNCHRONOUS entity is a variable. PENDING R802/8.6.3 source-use of proper declarations; an I/O-free declaration is not an execution oracle and no new no-op S classifier is created.

Fortran asynchronous I/O has its12.5/12.6/12.7 connection, constant-YES initiation, storage-sequence, completion and error conditions. The processor may perform the operation synchronously under12.6.2.5p3; the attribute is not a promise of overlap, latency or a required nonzero ID.

The other branch is18.10.4 communication through procedures defined other than by Fortran. Which procedures initiate/complete it is processor dependent. PENDING genuine processor/interface documentation; neither ordinary Fortran stubs, thread/coarray activity, I/O WAIT nor an MPI-looking name establishes this protocol.
PDF120 lines22-26 is one conditional prose obligation with two conjuncts, three usage alternatives and two kinds of pending affector. It is not a new numbered diagnostic policy.
9.4.2p3 defines the base object of a data-ref through the leftmost part name. Do not replace it by an arbitrary component or infer all target attributes from pointer ownership.
A specification occurrence need not be a value reference or nonconstant expression; inquiry and value-use premises remain distinct.

Some statement of that scope executes while the variable is a pending affector. It is not necessary that the particular occurrence of the variable be the statement executed during the pending interval.
12.6.2.5p5/p6 defines the pending storage sequence and any-part storage association, including SIZE storage and possibly noncontiguous sets.
18.10.4 defines the processor-qualified initiation/completion interval and any-part association for communication affectors.
Both the scope usage condition and executed-while-pending condition must hold. Attribute presence alone does not prove either event.

PDF120 lines27-28 identifies the implicit attribute route whose exact conditions are defined in12.6.2.5p4. This cross-reference does not create another local S obligation or make that canonical implication optional.

PENDING finite canonical route matrix: an I/O-list variable, each namelist group object and a SIZE= variable in an asynchronous transfer. Their data-ref base objects are the subjects; a namelist group name itself is not the buffer variable.

The implication applies in the data-transfer statement's scoping unit and may be explicitly confirmed. Removing a declaration while leaving the implicit route does not make a missing-attribute negative. Attribute presence is not a flag that automatically vanishes after WAIT.

PENDING12.6.2.5p4 source-use with R1213/C1225's constant ASYNCHRONOUS value and the SIZE/NML restrictions. ID/IOSTAT/IOMSG are not added to the pending storage set merely because they are I/O controls; keep their storage disjoint from the transfer variables. No new graph entry or facet credit.
Original physical PDF121, printed107, lines1-6: association permission, the nonlocal BLOCK specification effect and subobject propagation. It is paragraph4, not a fabricated continuation-note unit.

An object with ASYNCHRONOUS may be associated with one without it. PENDING exact argument/use/host contexts; this does not waive type/kind/rank, explicit-interface, VALUE, definability, contiguity or pending-affector restrictions.

14.2.2p2/p9/p10 permit specific local attribute differences and constrain multiple use paths. PENDING finite same-object use-associated examples, not a new object or unqualified attribute mismatch policy.

19.5.1.4 and8.8 govern host availability and permitted local ASYNCHRONOUS specification. PENDING a known host variable with no local redeclaration; do not infer that an ordinary type declaration merely changes the host object's attribute rather than shadowing it.
The single unnumbered NOTE on PDF121 explains pending storage and possible code-motion use. It is not a continuation of the ALLOCATABLE note and supplies no independent optimization obligation.
The storage sequence concerns the operation's actual storage units and may be noncontiguous; no allocator layout or contiguous-buffer assumption follows.
The explanation is tied to the scoping unit and pending operation, not unrestricted background mutation or an always-active attribute.

The compiler could use the information to inhibit certain code motion. This does not require a particular optimization pass, a hardware memory barrier, a thread model, an execution-time speedup or a sleep-based oracle.

requirements.title: Used pending-affector variables require scoped ASYNCHRONOUS base objects
requirements.definition: The base object needs ASYNCHRONOUS in a scoping unit when the variable is a dummy argument or occurs in an executable statement or specification expression there, and some statement of that scope executes while the variable is a pending I/O storage-sequence affector or pending communication affector. The two conditions are separate: an occurrence only after completion can still satisfy the usage condition. Pending status and storage overlap come from the defining I/O/communication rules, not elapsed time, attribute presence or the spelling of a call.

pending.dummy-pending-input: PENDING complete source/operational-control plan with a live INTEGER buffer and an explicit-interface ASYNCHRONOUS assumed-shape dummy. Initiate valid asynchronous input outside the finishing procedure; the finishing scope waits successfully before reading the dummy and checking independent17/23. No VALUE or INTENT(OUT), hidden premature value copy, vector-subscript actual or expired local buffer. Attribute necessity still requires the actual pending-affector/scoping proof, not a mere declaration.
pending.dummy-pending-output: PENDING corresponding output context with a defined buffer17/23 and an ASYNCHRONOUS dummy, complete interface and compatible type/kind/rank. Keep the buffer defined and unchanged until completion; only afterward reuse it. Output may be referenced while pending, but not redefined, undefined or pointer-reassociated. Do not apply the stricter input no-reference rule to every output use.
pending.executable-scope-input: PENDING source-use of a known nondummy base object occurring in a scope's executable statements, with a valid pending input interval and ASYNCHRONOUS in that scope. The occurrence need not itself run during the interval. Any actual argument association before completion must avoid VALUE, INTENT(OUT) and prohibited temporaries; do not read the input data to create the witness.
pending.executable-scope-output: PENDING finite output-affector context in which a nondummy live scalar/array is referenced by an executable statement while output is pending. Preserve the original defined value through completion and distinguish permitted reference from forbidden redefinition/undefinition. A disjoint scratch variable can carry other work; no race or timing requirement.
pending.specification-scope-input: PENDING source-qualified scope with a known fixed-shape INTEGER buffer used in a SIZE specification inquiry while a corresponding input operation is pending, with a statement of that scope executed during the pending interval. Only the already defined shape is inquired about; no element value, unavailable bound, deferred parameter or optional/INTENT(OUT) value. Retain the distinction between an occurrence and a data-value reference, and keep the proof documentary until all inquiry/affector premises are checked.
pending.specification-scope-output: PENDING a defined pending-output INTEGER affector used as an eligible scalar specification-expression value in a separate complete scope. Use nonoptional non-OUT dummy or valid host/use association and prior typing; preserve ASYNCHRONOUS there. Reads of defined output data are not the prohibited input case. Do not use an ordinary unrelated local value that is not a restricted expression.
pending.overlap-and-base-object: PENDING finite source map of a whole buffer, overlapping constant-index sections and a derived object's ordinary data component. Any-part association with the pending storage sequence matters; the data-ref base object is identified through its leftmost name. Do not infer pointer-target subobject membership, assume contiguity of the pending storage set, or claim that a seemingly disjoint update is legal without the full affector/definition analysis.
pending.io-completion-controls: PENDING canonical Clause12 operational controls, not attribute-only effects. Open scratch external sequential unformatted connections with ASYNCHRONOUS=YES and ACTION=READWRITE. Input sequence: synchronously write the defined two-INTEGER record17/23, REWIND, set the input buffer to-1/-2, initiate asynchronous READ with ID/IOSTAT, WAIT successfully, then independently require17/23. Output sequence: write the defined buffer17/23 asynchronously, WAIT, overwrite the source buffer only after completion, REWIND and synchronously read back into separate storage for17/23 checks. Check every OPEN/transfer/positioning/WAIT/close status; the intended WAIT precedes later statements that could implicitly wait. A successful ID may be0; never require a positive ID, PENDING=true, actual overlap, sleeps or a capability skip.
pending.communication-input: PENDING processor/interface gate for one genuine non-Fortran initiation/completion pair recognized under18.10.4, with a live input variable and exact participating scopes/aliases. No input-affector reference, definition, undefinition, VALUE association or pointer-association change in the interval. A Fortran stub, arbitrary callback, coarray synchronization, MPI-looking name or I/O WAIT is not proof of that protocol.
pending.communication-output: PENDING the same independently identified foreign-procedure protocol for a defined output variable, allowing only operations permitted during output communication. Preserve no redefinition/undefinition/association change until the actual completion procedure. Processor identification and compatible interfaces are missing evidence here; no C/MPI fixture, profile, install or compiler assumption is supplied.
pending.absent-conjuncts-source-use: PENDING finite source truth table: declaration only with no dummy/executable/specification occurrence; usage but no pending operation; a pending interval with no statement of that scope executed; and both conjuncts established. Absence of this obligation does not forbid ASYNCHRONOUS. I/O-free admission establishes no operational coverage, and a physical transfer completing immediately does not prove all pending-status or attribute-necessity claims.
pending.missing-attribute-policy-gate: PENDING source-only omission contrast in a separate participating scope with no inherited or implicit ASYNCHRONOUS route, repaired solely by the appropriate explicit attribute specification. Use module-provided interfaces so the repair does not leave a conflicting interface body. Removing a keyword while an I/O-list/NML/SIZE implication remains is not a negative. Do not execute a nonconforming race or demand a diagnostic without a separately justified policy/canonical numbered condition.

requirements.oracle: Original source establishes the complete conjunction and affector lifetimes. Proposed operational controls require successful external connection, initiation and completion, defined independent post-WAIT values, disjoint unit/ID/status storage and complete interfaces. They exercise legitimate I/O but do not automatically prove every attribute-necessity predicate or simultaneous hardware execution. For foreign communication, processor-recognized procedure roles and interface evidence are a prerequisite.
requirements.oracle_limitation: All twelve facets remain pending. This prose obligation has no invented mandatory diagnostic or optional-capability skip. C1225/C1226/C1227, C1546-C1549 and other numbered conditions retain their own required-reporting owners and exact subjects. Actual data movement may be synchronous, a successful ID may be0, and errors may be reported at initiation or completion. On a failed operation, report the specific stage/status and do not read an undefined ID, SIZE variable or input buffer, or continue using indeterminate file position. I/O environment failures are not automatically attribute violations. No arbitrary timing, storage-layout, VOLATILE, thread, coarray or generic memory-barrier oracle.

requirements.title: A BLOCK can give a nonlocal object scoped ASYNCHRONOUS
requirements.source: 8.5.4 p4 middle sentence, physical PDF121, printed107, lines2-5
requirements.definition: When an object that is not a local variable of a BLOCK is specified ASYNCHRONOUS in that construct's specification-part, the object has the attribute within the construct even if it lacks it outside. This is a scoped property of the same object, not a new local variable, allocation, SAVE implication or hardware fence. The outer object may already have the attribute; outside absence is not a mandatory premise.

pending.same-nonlocal-object: PENDING finite source-use of one previously declared outer INTEGER array named by ASYNCHRONOUS in a BLOCK, with outside-absent and outside-present attribute variants. Preserve object identity, type and shape; the special ASYNCHRONOUS statement does not create a new construct entity. A mere I/O-free declaration or nonexistent attribute-query intrinsic is not an execution oracle.
pending.nested-block-scope: PENDING outer/inner BLOCK source matrix with an explicit specification in only the inner block and proper name availability. Do not infer an attribute change in unrelated scopes or use an ordinary local type declaration that shadows the intended object. Complete all operations that use the localized pending region before leaving its required scope.
pending.use-and-host-object: PENDING finite contexts for a known use-associated object and a known host-associated object, retaining14.2.2/19.5.1.4 and IMPORT restrictions. Scope-local attribute differences are permitted but type/rank/argument and pending-affector requirements still apply. No blanket rule that associated objects must have identical ASYNCHRONOUS attributes.
pending.operational-block-io-control: PENDING canonical operational control with an outer defined buffer, BLOCK ASYNCHRONOUS specification, successful external asynchronous input and explicit successful WAIT inside the BLOCK, then independent17/23 checks on the outer object after exit. This can expose accidental shadowing, but the I/O statement also supplies an implicit attribute route; its data result alone does not isolate or complete this declaration-effect facet.
pending.argument-constraint-evidence-gate: PENDING original-owner C1548/C1549 evidence plan using eligible strided actual arrays/pointers and complete explicit-interface ASYNCHRONOUS dummies. Resolve whether the BLOCK-scoped attribute supplies the exact canonical constraint premise; keep minimal repairs to the selected dummy/contiguity condition. Such a compile diagnostic/control is not an I/O execution or a new S-negative. No wrapper, fixture or link is authored here.

requirements.oracle: A finite identity/scope and canonical-constraint plan. The effect category records the source's declaration semantics. Any future operational check must use actual I/O initiation/completion and independent defined values, and separately justify attribution to the scoped attribute rather than an implicit I/O route.
requirements.oracle_limitation: All five facets remain pending. The integrated SourceUses registry is empty and even reviewed inventories cannot grant facet-completion credit. No direct ASYNCHRONOUS inquiry exists in this plan; no no-op program, race, thread/barrier model, compiler timing or compile-only substitute is an effect oracle. The18.10.4 foreign-communication BLOCK example needs actual processor-recognized procedures, not a fabricated Fortran replacement.

requirements.title: ASYNCHRONOUS propagates to the object's subobjects
requirements.source: 8.5.4 p4 final sentence, physical PDF121, printed107, lines5-6
requirements.definition: An object's ASYNCHRONOUS attribute also belongs to all of its subobjects. Subobject identity follows the original object/designator rules, not arbitrary storage reachability: a pointer component in a pointer-association context differs from the target to which it refers. Storage-overlap affectors and per-scope base-object obligations remain separately governed by p2 and the I/O/communication rules.

pending.array-elements-sections: PENDING finite source-use of an ASYNCHRONOUS ordinary INTEGER array's element, contiguous section and constant-triplet strided section. Preserve genuine subobject status and canonical C1548 conditions if an argument-association witness is later used. Do not require a contiguous pending storage sequence or infer permitted mutation from apparent nonoverlap alone.
pending.character-substrings: PENDING default-CHARACTER object/substrings source map plus a qualified canonical formatted READ control: prepare record ABCD, read two characters with explicit A2 format and ADVANCE=NO on an external ASYNCHRONOUS=YES connection, wait successfully, then require AB and SIZE count2. SIZE and the input substring must not be observed while pending. This is not a raw source-byte/display-shape or timing oracle.
pending.nested-data-components: PENDING a complete derived object with ordinary scalar/array data components, including nested data components; give the containing object ASYNCHRONOUS and resolve each selected data subobject. An allocatable component must be allocated with needed parameters/shape before an I/O value use and remain alive through completion. Its initial unallocated status and deallocation behavior stay with7.5.4.6/9.7.
pending.base-object-pointer-boundary: PENDING finite9.4.2p3/p5 source contrast for object%pointer as a pointer component versus dereferencing its target. The leftmost base object and genuine subobject relation are different questions. Do not automatically propagate the containing object's attribute to an independently declared target or procedure entity; separately analyze any alias that becomes a pending storage/communication affector.
pending.argument-and-io-evidence-gate: PENDING canonical source/case relations between inherited subobject attributes, C1548/C1549 argument constraints and the three implicit I/O routes: list item, namelist group object and SIZE variable. A finite namelist control can synchronously write defined17/23, reset its data objects before asynchronous input, wait, then check17/23. No namelist-format plus item-list combination, SIZE in namelist/list-directed I/O, invalid dummy copy or unallocated payload. Existing canonical owners remain, with no new local coverage from declarations alone.

requirements.oracle: The original subobject relation and scoped attribute determine the proposed semantic evidence. Actual I/O controls require successful transfer/completion and independently expected values/counts; canonical argument diagnostics require their complete type/rank/attribute/contiguity premises. Neither is silently re-owned as automatic local effect coverage.
requirements.oracle_limitation: All five facets remain pending. No unallocated value/bounds/deferred-parameter read, pointer-target identity guess, ALLOCATED(pointer), VALUE association of pending input, early SIZE read or mutation of a pending affector. SourceUses has no execution or facet credit, and no inventory/graph/link is added. Optional processor scheduling is not permission to skip required language behavior or substitute a race-based test.
